item.title: MetaCaster: Meta-Harness-Optimized Agent for End-to-End Few-Shot Learning of Lightweight Time Series Forecasters
item.description: Time series forecasting (TSF) is evolving toward multimodal and agentic settings, yet using foundation models remains uneconomical in resource-constrained scenarios, where compact, specialized forecasters are more desirable. However, lightweight forecasters typically require substantial training data, limiting their use in domains with scarce, slowly accumulated, or privacy-sensitive time series. item.title: MomADv2: Reliable Temporal Memory for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
item.description: Long-horizon planning is critical for safe autonomous driving in complex scenarios. Existing methods improve planning continuity with temporal memory, but such memory may become invalid and mislead decisions when the driving command changes. Thus, selectively leveraging useful history while suppressing command-inconsistent memory remains a key challenge. item.title: First Demonstration of Multi-Agent LLM System for Million-Scale Optical Link Management in Global Production AIDCs
item.description: We present the first LLM-powered multi-agent system for autonomous fault management across millions of optical links in production AIDCs. Refined via SFT and continuous memory evolution, it achieves 97.7% F1 and over 60% fault-incident reduction, outperforming SOTA LLMs on a ten-week field data evaluation.

item.title: Beyond Surface Cues: Disentangling Sociocultural Signals in Multilingual LLMs
item.description: Multilingual LLM outputs can vary across sociocultural contexts. However, evidence of cultural grounding can be misleading: identity labels may be inferred from explicit or indirect textual cues, while names and wording can reveal the source language. item.description: Agent ecosystems now include thousands of MATS components (Models, Agents, Tools, and Skills), yet their discovery still relies on in-context routing. item.title: HANSARD: A Reference Architecture for Forensic Readiness, Runtime Witnessing, and Graded Attribution in Autonomous Multi-Agent AI Systems
item.description: Autonomous multi-agent systems nowadays act in finance, software supply chains, and security operations. item.description: Function calling represents the core capability of agentic large language models (LLMs).
